questions.prompt: Which beginning-of-construction date should govern the deal: off-site transformer manufacture from December 22, 2025, or on-site physical work from January 12, 2026?
questions.context: The seller relies on off-site physical work on a custom transformer under a binding contract dated December 10, 2025, supported only by the manufacturer's letter. The independent engineer has not reviewed the manufacturer's records and confirms on-site work began January 12, 2026. A 2025 start keeps the domestic content bonus (47.8% clears the 45% threshold) and keeps the prohibited foreign entity rules out of scope. A 2026 start loses the domestic content bonus (50% threshold) and brings those rules into play, with the module certification and cost ratio still missing. With prevailing wage and apprenticeship met, a 2026 start cuts the rate to 40% and the credit to $54,560,000 on $136,400,000 of basis.

evidence.text: Physical manufacture of the transformer, beginning with cutting and stacking of the custom core, commenced at our facility on December 22, 2025 and continued thereafter.
On-site physical work of a significant nature, beginning with pile installation for the tracker foundations, commenced on January 12, 2026.
We have not reviewed the manufacturer's records and express no opinion on the tax treatment of off-site work.
If construction is determined to have begun in 2026, the applicable threshold would be 50% and the Project would not qualify at the computed adjusted percentage.
No material assistance cost ratio calculation has been prepared.
